comment: Parametric gym equipment in metres. Every exercise reuses these definitions; nothing here is specific to the bench press. 'source' says where a dimension comes from. IPF = International Powerlifting Federation Technical Rulebook 2026 (PDF text read on 2026-11-11). Details of each check: bench-press/reference_notes.json.

barbell_olympic_20kg.source: IPF rulebook: total length not exceeding 2.2 m; 1.31 to 1.32 m between collar faces; shaft 28 to 29 mm; sleeves 50 to 52 mm; ring marks 81 cm apart; bar and collars 25 kg with collars of 2.5 kg each. Sleeve length (0.415 m) and collar width (0.03 m) are not in the IPF rulebook: they match a manufacturer sheet for a 20 kg competition bar (Eleiko, weightlifting model).

plate_20kg.source: IPF rulebook: largest discs not more than 45 cm in diameter, hole 52 to 53 mm, discs of 20 kg and over at most 6 cm thick. The thickness used here is a modelling choice inside that limit. Competition discs are colour coded (20 kg blue); these are generic dark plates with a ring in the brand colour, not competition discs.

flat_bench_with_rack.source: IPF rulebook: flat surface at least 1.22 m long, 29 to 32 cm wide, 42 to 45 cm from the floor to the top of the pad; bar rests adjustable from 75 to 110 cm; at least 1.10 m between the insides of the bar rests; the head of the bench extends 22 cm (+/- 5 cm) beyond the centre of the uprights. The rulebook also requires attached safety stands, which this model does not have. Frame shape is an original design.

dumbbell_hex_12kg.source: Approximate dimensions of a common commercial 12-12.5 kg rubber hex dumbbell (handle 13 cm between heads, 32 mm grip). No standard defines dumbbell sizes; values are typical, not from one manufacturer's drawing.
